item_title: The sediment trap that no longer needs a calm day
item_introduction: A one-piece body and a reusable collar cut deployment time by a third and removed the joint that failed most often.
add_paragraph: The old trap had a glued collar. In two seasons it failed **eleven times**, usually in exactly the conditions where a failure is least convenient. The replacement is a single printed body with a collar that unscrews by hand and can be reused across deployments.

The practical numbers matter more than the design: deployment time fell from **34 minutes to 21** per station, and the trap can now be serviced from a small boat without lifting the whole mooring aboard. Material use per trap is down by 40%.

All nine stations switched over during the spring round. The design files, print settings and field-service checklist will be released with the next version of the sediment-flux dataset, once the first inter-comparison against the old design is complete.
